That is why it can natively be written in several passes — and these three buttons are split along exactly that semantics: ① Send (append): the first press issues AT+QISEND=0 to enter data mode, and every press after that appends one more chunk; ⚠ while already in data mode it does NOT reissue the command (reissuing it would be written in as data); ② Send then finish automatically: append this chunk and add Ctrl+Z right away, done in one go; ③ Finish (Ctrl+Z): sends only the terminator, flushing everything accumulated so far in one shot. To give up midway, press ESC Cancel (0x1B). The terminal flags it when data mode is entered, and the three buttons light up as well. ⚠ The data itself must not contain 0x1A — the module would take it as an early finish; use Send Hex to send control characters.

The hex string is limited to 512 characters, which works out to 256 bytes of actual data (manual §2.3.10); for anything longer use Send Text above (1460 bytes). ⚠ That trailing 0A (newline) is not decoration: the default peer tcpbin.com is a "line-oriented" echo server, and until it sees a newline it just keeps buffering and sends nothing back — measured: sending Hello without 0A gave no response at all after 6 s, while appending a single 0A brought it back within 0.1 s. 收到 closed URC 時自動補送: Auto-send when a closed URC arrives
勾選後，只要偵測到 +QIURC: \"closed\",<id> 就自動送出對: When checked, every detected +QIURC: "closed",<id> automatically sends the matching AT+QICLOSE=<id>. The connectID comes from the URC itself, not hard-coded to 0. Why: after the peer closes, the socket sits in the closing state, and reopening without this step returns error 563 (socket identity already in use) — tcpbin.com has a 15 s idle timeout, so you hit this constantly while testing. The setting is kept in the browser (localStorage) and survives a reload
